description: The FCC's FM and TV propagation curves calculator is an online tool of the US Federal Communications Commission that applies the commission's CURVES program to estimate broadcast coverage. The page read on 2026-09-28 explains that the JavaScript calculator uses the F(50,50) curves for FM and analog television service, the F(50,10) curves for interfering signals and the F(50,90) curves for digital television service to find the distance to a service or interfering contour, or the field strength at a given distance, from the antenna height above average terrain and effective radiated power; heights can be taken from the FM and TV query tools or the HAAT calculator, printable curve graphs are offered, and the page defines the protected contours by FM station class (54, 57 or 60 dBu). Coverage is the United States regulatory framework. Access is free online; the code runs in the browser and no licence is stated. Caveats: the curves are statistical averages over terrain and ignore local obstructions, so they give regulatory, not exact coverage. It supports modelling the coverage of broadcast stations used for emergency alerting and the effect of losing a transmitter. Related records: data-fcc-antenna-structure-registration lists the towers.
